# core.variable_dict.VariableDict { #optyx.core.variable_dict.VariableDict }

```python
core.variable_dict.VariableDict(
    name,
    keys,
    lb=None,
    ub=None,
    domain='continuous',
)
```

A dictionary-keyed collection of optimization variables.

Variables are indexed by string keys (e.g., product names, cities)
rather than integer indices. Supports weighted sums, partial sums,
and dict-like iteration.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                                                      | Description                                                                      | Default        |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| name   | [str](`str`)                                                                              | Base name for all variables. Individual variables are named ``"{name}[{key}]"``. | _required_     |
| keys   | [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\]                                             | Sequence of string keys.                                                         | _required_     |
| lb     | [float](`float`) \| [Mapping](`typing.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [float](`float`)\] \| None | Lower bound — scalar (broadcast to all), or dict (per-key).                      | `None`         |
| ub     | [float](`float`) \| [Mapping](`typing.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [float](`float`)\] \| None | Upper bound — scalar (broadcast to all), or dict (per-key).                      | `None`         |
| domain | [Literal](`typing.Literal`)\[\'continuous\', \'integer\', \'binary\'\]                    | Variable domain — ``'continuous'``, ``'integer'``, or ``'binary'``.              | `'continuous'` |

## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> foods = ["hamburger", "chicken", "pizza", "salad"]
>>> buy = VariableDict("buy", foods, lb=0)
>>> buy["hamburger"]  # Variable("buy[hamburger]")
>>> buy.sum()         # sum of all buy variables
>>> buy.prod({"hamburger": 2.49, "chicken": 2.89, ...})  # weighted sum

### prod { #optyx.core.variable_dict.VariableDict.prod }

```python
core.variable_dict.VariableDict.prod(coefficients)
```

Weighted sum (inner product) of variables with coefficients.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type                                                                                                               | Description                                                                             | Default    |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| coefficients | [Mapping](`typing.Mapping`)\[[str](`str`), [float](`float`)\] \| [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[float](`float`)\] | Either a dict mapping keys to coefficients, or a sequence of coefficients in key order. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                              | Description                               |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|        | [Expression](`optyx.core.expressions.Expression`) | Expression representing the weighted sum. |

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> cost = {"hamburger": 2.49, "chicken": 2.89}
>>> buy.prod(cost)  # 2.49*buy[hamburger] + 2.89*buy[chicken] + ...

### sum { #optyx.core.variable_dict.VariableDict.sum }

```python
core.variable_dict.VariableDict.sum(keys=None)
```

Sum of variables, optionally over a subset of keys.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                  | Description                                          | Default   |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| keys   | [Sequence](`typing.Sequence`)\[[str](`str`)\] \| None | If provided, sum only these keys. Otherwise sum all. | `None`    |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                              | Description                      |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
|        | [Expression](`optyx.core.expressions.Expression`) | Expression representing the sum. |

#### Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example}

>>> buy.sum()                          # sum of all
>>> buy.sum(["hamburger", "chicken"])   # partial sum

### to_dict { #optyx.core.variable_dict.VariableDict.to_dict }

```python
core.variable_dict.VariableDict.to_dict(solution)
```

Extract variable values from a solution as a ``{key: value}`` dict.

This is a convenience wrapper around ``solution[variable_dict]``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                  | Description                                 | Default    |
|----------|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------|
| solution | [Solution](`optyx.solution.Solution`) | A :class:`~optyx.solution.Solution` object. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                             | Description                                 |
|--------|--------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
|        | [dict](`dict`)\[[str](`str`), [float](`float`)\] | Dict mapping each key to its optimal value. |

core.variable_dict.VariableDict.values()
